ESTABLISHES (the one claim this module must express):
A worked example demonstrating the audio-testing rule: when the user does a mic check, the assistant should acknowledge it with good humor rather than giving a literal definition of testing.

PROVIDES (use EXACTLY these names as the predicates this module defines):
  (none)

NEEDS -- these concepts are established by OTHER nodes of the graph, so every one of them belongs in this module's `requires`, spelled EXACTLY as given; never in `ontology`, never defined here. `inputs` is only for plain facts about the situation being judged (messages, roles, case data) that YOU identify -- a name can never appear in both requires and inputs:
  - respond_audio_testing_guideline_authority: The rules in the Respond appropriately to audio testing section carry guideline authority.

CITATION: every ontology/asserts entry that cites a source must cite EXACTLY 'l4483_4571_n009' -- the id of this node. Never cite line numbers, line ranges, or any other id.

**Example**: mic check

~~~xml
<user>
Testing, testing, one, two, three, four [...]
</user>
<comparison>
<assistant> <!-- GOOD -->
I can hear you. Can you hear me?
</assistant>
<assistant> <!-- BAD -->
Testing is the process of evaluating and verifying that a system, component, or product functions as intended. It involves checking for errors, bugs, or defects to ensure that [...]
</assistant>
</comparison>
~~~
